rules.name: Capstone Options
rules.desc: All students must choose one of the following 3 options to meet the Capstone requirement. More information about this requirement can be found on the department website.

children.name: Capstone Option #1- Honors
10 units of BIO 199 or BIO 199X in the honors lab
Approved honors proposal, symposium presentation and honors thesis approved by two readers
3.0 GPA in Biology major requirements taken at Stanford

children.notes:
Course Requirements:

• 10 units of BIO 199 or BIO 199X (must submit BIO 199X petition) from your Honors lab completed during your junior and senior years only. 7 of the 10 units of BIO 199 or BIO 199X can double count toward additional electives requirement.

• If this poses a challenge, we will consider exceptions on a case-by-case basis for students who have completed comparable experience through federal work study, paid research experience, etc.

• 3 units of BIO 199W. Fulfills WIM. BIO 199W can double count toward additional electives requirement.
To graduate with departmental honors, a student must conduct an independent research project during their junior and senior years. Research must be done in a Biology Department lab or a lab in another department for which the student has obtained prior approval.
Administrative steps include:

• Submit an approved honors proposal during the winter quarter of junior year.

• Complete at least ten units of an approved research project from the same lab. Students conducting research in a lab outside of the Department of Biology must submit an Out of Department Research Petition either before they start their research or, if the research was started before declaring the Biology major, as soon as their major declaration is approved. Only research units from BIO are counted toward the ten-unit requirement.

• Obtain at least a 3.0 (B) grade point average (GPA) in all Biology major requirements taken at Stanford (foundational, breadth, and elective courses).

• Participate in the annual Achauer Undergraduate Biology Honors Symposium by presenting a poster or giving an oral presentation. The symposium is typically held in mid-May.

• Complete and, by the published deadline during the spring quarter of senior year, submit online an honors thesis approved by at least two readers. At least one reader must be from the faculty of the Department of Biology, and both readers must be Academic Council members. The title page of the honors thesis must include the student name, thesis title, name and department of research sponsor, and name and department of the second reader. Students must submit this page with original ink signatures to the student services office by the published deadline for the quarter in which graduation is expected.
Honors Program and Undergraduate Research in Biology for further information on the honors program.

children.name: Capstone Option #2- Independent Capstone
children.notes:
Students who wish to complete an independent capstone project must enroll in the Independent Capstone in Biology course series. Such projects might involve creative works, research or business internships, travel-based study, teaching, or community service. Examples include the production of a teaching or business plan, a film or podcast, or a public education campaign.
Students will enroll in Bio 199A and Bio 199B to complete the capstone requirement. Students will have two opportunities to enroll in the Independent Capstone requirement (one starting in spring of junior year and the later cohort starting in winter of senior year).

• BIO 199A–3 units

• Cohort A: enroll during spring quarter of the junior year

• Cohort B: enroll during winter quarter of senior year

• BIO 199B–3 units

• Cohort A: enroll during autumn quarter of senior year

• Cohort B: enroll during spring quarter of senior year
Students can view the full requirement information on the Independent Capstone and Virtual Showcase for past student projects.

children.name: Capstone Option #3- Notation in Science Communication
children.desc:
The Notation in Science Communication (NSC) provides undergraduates with a new opportunity to develop their ability to communicate technical information to a variety of audiences using multiple genres and modes. Through a combination of coursework, advising and reflection, selected students can earn a special designation on their official transcripts that indicates their advanced work in science communication. Students can submit an application through the Program in Writing and Rhetoric.
Note that students must fulfill all the requirements for the Notation in Science Communication in order to fulfill the capstone requirement.

children.name: PWR Elective Courses
children.desc: Students must complete one of the PWR 91 courses listed or a PWR194 course that is tagged for the specific notation (aside from PWR 91NSC, which is already required).
children.notes: See NSC Overview for specific approved courses.

children.name: Non-PWR Elective Course
children.desc:
An additional (3-5 unit) non-PWR elective course is required to complete the Notation in Science Communication.
This website lists sample courses that could qualify as non-PWR elective courses. Students must email notationsc@stanford.edu with their choice of elective course, whether that course is on this list or not, in order for that course to count toward their progress in the Notation. If you have questions about the non-PWR Elective course requirement, email notationsc@stanford.edu.
children.notes: WIM courses may not double- count towards both the department and NSC requirements.

rules.name: Honors

children.name: 10 units of BIO research (BIO 199 or BIO 199X) in one lab
Approved honors proposal, symposium presentation and honors thesis approved by two readers
3.0 GPA in Biology major requirements taken at Stanford

rules.desc:
To graduate with departmental honors, a student must conduct an independent research project, typically over the course of at least one year; projects are started no later than Autumn Quarter of the junior year. Research must be done in a Biology Department lab or a lab in another department for which the student has obtained prior approval. Administrative steps include:

• Submit an approved honors proposal during the Winter quarter a year before intended graduation.

• Complete at least 10 units of an approved research project in the same lab. Students conducting research in a lab outside of the Department of Biology must submit an Out of Department Research Petition either before they start their research, or if research was started prior to declaring the Biology major, as soon as their major declaration is approved. Only research units from BIO counted toward the 10 unit requirement.

• Obtain at least a 3.0 (B) grade point average (GPA) in all Biology major requirements taken at Stanford (foundational, breadth, and elective courses).

• If graduating in Spring, participate in the annual Achauer Undergraduate Biology Honors Symposium by presenting a poster or giving an oral presentation. The symposium is typically held at the end of May.

• Complete and, by the published deadline within the quarter graduation is expected, submit online an honors thesis approved by at least two readers by the published deadline within the quarter graduation is expected. At least one reader must be from the faculty of the Department of Biology, and both readers must be Academic Council members. The title page of the honors thesis must include student's name, thesis title, name and department of research sponsor, and name and department of second reader. Students must submit this page with original ink signatures to the student services office by the published deadline for the quarter in which graduation is expected.
Further information on the honors program is available on the Honors Program and Undergraduate Research in Biology website.

gpa: All Biology courses must be passed with a D- or better when taken for a letter grade.
grading:
All Biology courses must be passed with a D- or better when taken for a letter grade. Students can take 1 Credit/No Credit course in the STEM section and 1 Credit/No Credit course for their electives section of their subplan (Satisfactory/No credit courses do not count as Credit/No credit and are treated like letter grade courses).
Should a student take more than one CR/NC course in the STEM section of the subplan before declaring Biology, they will not be allowed to have a 1 Credit/No credit course for their electives
policies: Department degree policies can be accessed in our Biology Handbook. Students interested in studying abroad can find more information in our Studying Away from Stanford.
transferPolicy:
Students are encouraged to have courses outside Stanford evaluated before taking that course at another institution. Course catalogs, syllabi, papers, exams, and lecture notes from other institutions are necessary for evaluation and accreditation. Transfer students are encouraged to contact the Student Services Office soon after arrival and with the Director of the Transfer Advising Program to review major requirements. Incoming transfer students can submit a Transfer Credit Evaluation form during the summer, but it will not be reviewed until the start of the Autumn quarter.
Students are encouraged to review the pre-approved course lists outlined by the Stanford University-wide Transfer Credit Database and Biology pre-approved transfer courses. The department authorizes transfer credit only for courses whose content parallels the Stanford courses and has comparable prerequisites (not merely a comparable course title). If transfer course(s) are not already approved at the university or department level, students should submit a Transfer Credit Evaluation Form. For full detailed transfer credit instructions, please visit the Biology Transfer Credit website.
Biology students cannot use transfer credit or other external credit to substitute their BIO 40 and 80-series requirements (exemption: transfer students with an approved Transfer Credit Evaluation petition).
Credit for natural history, cultural biology, and similar courses is rarely appropriate and can be obtained only by meeting the same criteria outlined above. Verification of performance and the number of units is determined after completing the course. In some cases, students must provide exams, reading lists, term papers, and other materials for the evaluation.
reviewNotes: With no subplan you follow General Biology: four BioFoundations courses, the two foundational labs, math, physics, chemistry and statistics, and 23 units of electives. Each subplan instead has its own foundations, STEM courses and electives, drawing on its Menu I list plus the Biology and approved out-of-department lists, with at most one extra BIO 80-series course, one extra lab and 7 units of BIO 199/199X. The audit counts your courses toward 89 units. The capstone is honors (10 research units, BIO 199W, a thesis and a 3.0 GPA), the Independent Capstone, the Notation in Science Communication, or interdisciplinary honors (checked by hand). Left: only one STEM course and one elective may be taken Credit/No Credit, which the audit does not limit, and BIO 102's stated 4 units exceed its 3-unit listing, so only the course is required.
